METHODOLOGY_MOVIE_DESYNC_ROOT_CAUSE_2026.trigger: Operator watched a real 60Hz playback of D17_Goldberry.movie.json at the operator's request ('recoreded two videos ... Do your thing now') and immediately identified visible desync ('yeah, still desyncs'), even after an initial (wrong) hypothesis that it was specifically an advanceToFrame-vs-60Hz regime gap.
METHODOLOGY_MOVIE_DESYNC_ROOT_CAUSE_2026.actual_root_cause: The isolated instance had been launched all session via the GENERIC fork launcher (scripts/debugger-client/launch_debugger_instance.sh), which writes a minimal settings.ini with NO [CPU] section and does not seed the memory card the movies were recorded against. tools/launch_repro_playback.sh exists specifically to fix this -- it owns a determinism-matched settings.ini (explicit [CPU] ExecutionMode, FastmemMode, overclock-disabled, etc.) and seeds a pristine memory-card snapshot fresh on every launch. This is documented in the script's own header comments but had not been applied to this row's investigation until the operator's direct observation forced the check.
METHODOLOGY_MOVIE_DESYNC_ROOT_CAUSE_2026.fix: Relaunched via: tools/launch_repro_playback.sh --config-dir /tmp/dsrepro-d17 --port 23514 --token debugger-1000 --execution-mode Interpreter --disc <pristine .cue>. Verified the resulting settings.ini has ExecutionMode=Interpreter under [CPU] (the script's own 'READY ... (CachedInterpreter, card-seeded)' success message is a stale/hardcoded string in the script and does NOT reflect the actual configured mode -- read settings.ini directly to confirm, not the console message).
METHODOLOGY_MOVIE_DESYNC_ROOT_CAUSE_2026.confirmation: Same movie, same real-60Hz-resume playback, on the corrected instance: operator confirmed 'syncs properly now'. A controlled RAM-hash + position comparison between advanceToFrame-only replay and a replay that switched to real debugger.resume for a window (done BEFORE the launcher fix was found) had already shown measurable divergence (Flik position off by ~1500 units, differing SHA-256 of the full 2MB RAM image at the same nominal frame) -- consistent with, though not a clean isolation of, the same underlying problem.
METHODOLOGY_MOVIE_DESYNC_ROOT_CAUSE_2026.consequence_for_prior_data: All state reads taken on the mis-launched instance are suspect and were re-verified on the corrected instance before being trusted. The one specific finding that changed materially: an early trace of id=30's hp across the WHOLE D17_Goldberry movie on the mis-launched instance showed hp constant at 50 throughout (i.e., no combat happened) -- re-run identically on the corrected instance, the SAME movie shows a full, real combat sequence (two hits landed on Flik, nine hits landing on the bird, hp 50->18, a state transition). The desync was not cosmetic -- it was silently discarding the actual recorded gameplay content while `movie.status.reproducible` reported true throughout.
METHODOLOGY_MOVIE_DESYNC_ROOT_CAUSE_2026.standing_lesson: For ANY movie-replay work on this project, use tools/launch_repro_playback.sh, not the generic fork launcher, regardless of whether the replay will be instrumented (accessLog/execTrace) or watched purely for gameplay/visual state. The generic launcher's missing [CPU] section is sufficient on its own to desync movie replay; this is a broader and more silent problem than the already-documented arm-phase and CPU-execution-mode-forcing issues, because `movie.status.reproducible` does NOT detect it.

Live data in both movies shows id30's hp dropping in a steady staircase (D17_Goldberry: 50->46->42->38->34->30->26->22->18, roughly -4 per hit; D17.movie.json: 50->48->...->22->20) while id30's own position stays fixed and Flik's position is not tracked as approaching it -- consistent with an automated, non-thrown projectile source rather than a manual aimed hit. The exact -4-per-hit amount matches the already-established generic hit-tail 'gold class' damage documented elsewhere this session (class 11 -> -4), though whether the shooter plant's projectile is literally gold-class or an independently-tuned fixed value was not traced to the exact instruction this pass.
COMBAT_SEQUENCE_2026-08-02.descend_then_reattack: Operator: the bird starts to descend after ~f4650. Matches live data: id30's Y returns from -143376 back to -60832 right around f4650-4700 in D17_Goldberry.movie.json. hp does not begin dropping until just after this point (first drop observed at f4825 in the original sampling pass, consistent with the shooter's projectiles only being able to connect once the bird is back in range).
COMBAT_SEQUENCE_2026-08-02.DEFEAT_IS_A_THRESHOLD_NOT_HP_ZERO: The central mechanical finding this pass. In BOTH movies, hp does NOT reach 0 -- it freezes at a value in the 18-22 range (D17.movie.json: freezes at 20, at f2330; D17_Goldberry.movie.json: freezes at 18, at f5060) and, in the SAME frame as the freeze, id30's vm_ip jumps from its circling program (0x8007788c) to a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT part of the shared mover-VM bytecode blob (0x800776ac 'park_arrive_stop' / 0x800776ae 'jump_back', looping between the two -- confirmed against analysis/vm_programs.md, which happens to label this address range under an unrelated species, '## redbug @ 0x80077690'; this is a generic reusable primitive, not evidence id30 becomes a redbug). flags also change sharply at the same frame. Operator confirms this state IS 'defeated' -- the level-complete results screen appearing shortly after in D17_Goldberry.movie.json (grain 24/50, an unlabeled 0/4 counter, an unlabeled 00/09 counter) is proof of this, not evidence the encounter was left unresolved as an earlier draft of this finding wrongly concluded before the operator corrected it.

This directly resolves the row's own 'retreat/re-engage' missing item, at least for the retreat half; whether a 're-engage' is possible (does the bird ever return for a second fight in the same level session) was not tested this pass.

This is the actual hit/kill trigger, and it is the SAME generic contact-damage handler (0x8004A814, inside FUNC_8004A700 player_damage_handler) used for ordinary enemy hits elsewhere in the game, routed down its death path -- not a distinct bird-attack state.
CLIFFSIDE_HAZARD_ENCOUNTER_2026-08-02.POSITION_FIELD_CORRECTION_2026-08-02: CORRECTS an earlier claim in this same section ('id30's own record shows no change at this frame ... the kill is not reflected in the bird's own actor record at all'). That claim was reading the WRONG position field. The generic actor record actually carries TWO distinct position fields, confirmed by comparing them side by side on both this fixture and the Birdnest movies: +0x28/2c/30 is a TARGET/AI-setpoint position (jumps discretely at behavioral-state transitions -- e.g. the Birdnest gold-berry Y jump, or this actor's fixed Cliffside hover point) while +0x04/08/0c is the PHYSICALLY-INTERPOLATED current position (smoothly chases the target every frame; converges with it at major transitions, e.g. exactly at the Birdnest defeat freeze, f5060, where both fields read -67150). Re-reading id30's +0x04/08/0c (the physical field) through the Cliffside kill window shows a clean, steady dive at constant velocity from f300 (Y=-40800, delta -30037 from Flik) closing smoothly to a closest approach of just 1365 units above Flik at EXACTLY f327 -- two frames before the f329 hit. This is the bird's real attack: a physical stoop/dive strike, not an invisible proximity trigger. The Birdnest combat-sequence claims elsewhere in this artifact (COMBAT_SEQUENCE_2026-08-02) used +0x28/2c/30 throughout and remain valid AS READS OF THE TARGET FIELD -- they correctly tracked every behavioral-state transition (gold berry launch, descend, defeat) and are not retracted, but should be understood as target-setpoint reads, not literal continuous physical trajectory.
CLIFFSIDE_HAZARD_ENCOUNTER_2026-08-02.contact_caller_FUNC_8004ABF4: The caller that decides a Cliffside hit occurred (STILL_OPEN residual) is very likely FUNC_8004ABF4 (Canon: actor_player_contact_resolver / proximity_updater_8004abf4, span 0x8004ABF4-0x8004B6D8), which is confirmed to already be one of FUNC_8004A700's 6 statically-enumerated callers (via its 0x8004B4A0 call site, per FUNC_8004A700's own Canon page) and which -- per its OWN Canon doc -- iterates the live actor table at 0x80090748 doing per-actor proximity/contact dispatch against Flik. Live-confirmed this pass: id=30 occupies SLOT 0 of that table during the Cliffside encounter (0x80090748 itself, not an offset into it), which is exactly the single actor FUNC_8004ABF4's own partially-decoded entry math reads via G_TYPE6_ACTOR_PTR. However, that entry-math's specific radius/threshold check (dx^2+dy^2+dz^2 < r^2 using the +0x6a radius field and a -7360 Y-bias) evaluates to NOT-inside at every sampled frame including the closest approach (f327) -- so while the caller is now well-evidenced by actor-slot identity and call-graph membership, the EXACT branch/threshold inside this function's undecoded body that actually fires the contact is still not pinned. Not a full closure of that residual, but a substantial narrowing (from 'completely unknown' to 'this specific already-Canon function, exact branch TBD').
CLIFFSIDE_HAZARD_ENCOUNTER_2026-08-02.power_flags_bit_0x10_checked_not_found: Exhaustively checked this pass, still open. debugger.xrefsTo on 0x800A6590 (power-flags word) was run against BOTH the Birdnest (D17.movie.sav) and Cliffside (D17_Cliffside_Bird_Death.movie.sav) resident RAM images -- both return the SAME 8 static store sites (0x8001d5f8, 0x8004a7b0, 0x8004a8e0, 0x80051eb0, 0x80054e90, 0x8005b340, 0x8005d088, 0x800b3d3c), and every one was individually disassembled: none ORs in bit 0x10 (immediates found: 0x0001, 0x0002 x2, 0x0080, 0x0020 (andi), 0x0004 x2). A parallel grep of the entire hand-disassembled resident ASM corpus (asm/nonmatchings/resident/*.s, the 23 files that reference 0x6590) for an ori/andi immediate of 0x10 near a 0x6590 store also found nothing. The bit-0x10 writer is therefore almost certainly OVERLAY code specific to Cliffside (F04) that is not in the current disassembled corpus at all, or uses an addressing pattern (computed/indirect base) that a literal lui+offset static scan does not catch -- not a resident, already-documented writer being mis-attributed.
CLIFFSIDE_HAZARD_ENCOUNTER_2026-08-02.recovery_then_respawn: The stagger timer counts back up from -45 to 0 at a steady 1 tick per 2 frames (reaching 0 at f419, ~90 frames after the f329 hit -- the same tick rate documented for the invincibility timer at +0x7E elsewhere in this project). It then holds at exactly 0 for ~29 more frames (f419-447) while the screen visibly fades to black (captured screenshots: still mostly visible at f440, fully black by f447-449). At f448, lives (0x800A65A0) drops 9->8, Flik and id30 both teleport in lockstep to a new shared location (X/Z matching between them again, confirming the overhead-lock persists through the reposition), power-flags reset to 0x0, and the stagger timer resets to 35. Flik's true health (0x800A6594) stays constant at 4 throughout the ENTIRE sequence, including the death -- this hazard kills via a direct lives decrement + forced reposition, not by depleting health to 0. This directly satisfies the operator's framing: 'an enemy that attacks Flik if he lands on the ground.'
CLIFFSIDE_HAZARD_ENCOUNTER_2026-08-02.full_timeline: f192-194 land -> f300-327 physical dive-in (closing from 30037 units above Flik to 1365) -> f329 contact/death-branch fires (the hit, 2 frames after closest approach) -> f329-419 stagger recovers to 0 -> f419-447 black-screen transition -> f448 lives 9->8 + shared reposition + stagger/power-flags reset (the respawn commit).

SETPIECE_TRIGGER_WRITER_2026-08-02.method: Static-only, no movie needed: paused on a loaded save state (Birdnest, D17.movie.sav), ran debugger.xrefsTo on 0x800824dc (the setpiece spawn trigger), which returned all 24 static references (14 loads, 10 stores) in the currently-resident image. Disassembled every store site and cross-referenced the dispatch jump table at 0x8001b42c to confirm which kind index reaches the candidate.
SETPIECE_TRIGGER_WRITER_2026-08-02.result: The writer is the type-0x3f KIND-0x30 contact-action handler at 0x80054554-0x80054598, inside the already-documented FUNC_80053814 (type_0x3f_construct_contact_action_dispatch, source src_re/source3f_dispatch_80053814.c). Confirmed three independent ways: (1) xrefsTo surfaced the store at 0x80054574; (2) disassembly shows addiu v0,zero,-1 immediately before the store, guarded by bne v0,zero,skip (only fires while the trigger is currently idle/0 -- re-triggerable on every fresh approach, not a hard one-shot); (3) the kind-dispatch jump table 0x8001b42c[0x30-0x10] resolves to exactly 0x80054554, matching the pre-existing source comment's own kind-0x30 entry verbatim ('DEWDROP TELESCOPE / hint-view activation ... saves its ordinal to 0x800823cc, sets 0x800824dc, and clears player velocity/grounded state'). The same handler also writes fp (a running, unconditional per-entry loop counter over ALL type-3f records, confirmed via addu fp,zero,zero at function entry and addiu fp,fp,1 once per loop iteration) to 0x800823cc as the record index, and zeroes Flik's velocity (0x800A652C/6530/6534) and grounded/contact flags (0x800A6582) -- handing control to the camera-driven flyby.
SETPIECE_TRIGGER_WRITER_2026-08-02.cross_reference_is_the_new_part: The underlying decompilation already existed (source3f_dispatch_80053814.c's own header comment describes this kind-0x30 behavior in isolation) and this specific mechanism is independently corroborated by this project's existing green-gem-investigation memory ('Green gems = telescope hints, kind 0x30, entries 67/68/69'). What was missing, and is now supplied, is the explicit CROSS-REFERENCE connecting that kind-0x30 telescope handler to setpiece_spawn_8004d698.c's own open question ('the writer... is the SCRIPT/EVENT layer', never pinned to an instruction). This closes that STILL_OPEN item.
SETPIECE_TRIGGER_WRITER_2026-08-02.residual: This is a GENERIC hint/preview mechanism reused across the game (any kind-0x30 telescope entry can trigger ANY setpiece waypoint record, selected by the telescope's own loop-ordinal). Which specific telescope ordinal near Birdnest maps to the bird-flyby's specific waypoint record in table 0x80096dc8 was not traced this pass -- would need either a fixture spanning telescope-contact-through-flyby back to back, or a static LEVEL.DAT parse of Birdnest's type-3f entries filtered to kind 0x30 cross-referenced against that table's per-index content.
